title: Dual-Channel Variational Closure, Covariant Completion, and a Reproducible SPARC Benchmark
description: The dual-channel action F_dual(x) = 1/2 x^2 - x + ln(1+x) has constitutive ratio F'(x)/x equal to the MOND interpolation function mu(x) = x/(1+x). Given four structural constraints -- constitutive-relation form, Pade[1/1] minimality, the MOND boundary conditions, and dual-channel splitting -- F_dual is uniquely determined; the necessity of the Pade constraint is not derived, so the uniqueness is conditional. Embedded in the Skordis-Zlosnik (2021) RMOND framework, the linear screening ratio F''/F' approx 0.004 reduces a 76x structure overproduction to 0.4% in linear growth, and Vainshtein screening places the solar-system quadrupole at Q2 = 4.9e-29 s^-2, a factor 70 below the Cassini bound at natural O(1) couplings. Ghost-free with c_T = c. 17 Lean 4 modules verified, no sorry, axioms restricted to {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}. SPARC 175-galaxy benchmark; a0 = (1.116 +/- 0.161) x 10^-10 m/s^2. A pre-registered a0(z) test favours constant a0 over the horizon-tied a0(z) = xi c H(z) at 5.9 sigma, so the horizon interpretation of a0 is reported as disfavoured by the authors' own data.
